What medical expenses are covered if I get sick or injured abroad?

Section 1 pays, up to the limit in your Policy Schedule, the necessary and reasonable cost of medical, surgical and hospital treatment and ambulance costs if you become ill, are injured or die during the trip. It can also pay an earlier return ticket to the Philippines if medically necessary and approved by the Company (Section 1, p. 12).

Maaari ring sagutin ang mas maagang tiket pauwi ng Pilipinas kung kailangan ayon sa doktor at aprubado ng Kompanya (Section 1, p. 12).

Yes, if the illness or accident happened during the trip and initial treatment was received during the trip. Babayaran ng Kompanya ang bahaging hindi sagot ng limitasyon ng airline, hanggang sa limitang nasa Policy Schedule. Itinuturing na nawala ang bagahe matapos ang panahong itinakda ng carrier, hindi bababa sa 21 araw. I lost my passport abroad. What does the policy cover?

The cost to replace your passport, visa or non-refundable traveller's cheques, the travel needed to get the new documents, and accommodation until they are obtained if your trip goes past the planned return date, up to the plan limit. Meals are not included, and the loss must be reported within 24 hours (Section 16, p. 28).

What counts as a pre-existing condition?

Any illness or condition affecting you before your coverage started, including anything you got advice or treatment for, that was evident to you, or disclosed in the application. Within the 2-year look-back before purchase, any symptoms, consultation, test, diagnosis or medication change makes it pre-existing. Examples include hypertension, diabetes, asthma, heart disease, kidney disease and cancer (Definition 49, pp. 8-9).

Sa loob ng 2 taong look-back bago bumili, anumang sintomas, konsulta, test, diagnosis o pagbabago ng gamot ay ginagawa itong pre-existing. Halimbawa: altapresyon, diabetes, hika, sakit sa puso, sakit sa bato at kanser (Definition 49, pp. 8-9).

Some Hazardous Sports (e.g., off-road biking, canyoning, downhill skiing) may be covered for an extra premium (Definitions 16, 22 and 25, pp. 5-6).

Claims from travelling in, to or through a country or area where the Philippine Government issued a 'Do Not Travel' warning are excluded. The exception: if a place on your itinerary is added to the list after your policy was issued and before your trip starts, you may cancel or curtail under Trip Cancellation (General Exclusion 18, p. 35).
